summary.headline: Paramount Communications Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24.5% QoQ to INR 573 crore, but FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 117.5 crore (6% margin) on US tariff disruption.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sequential recovery: revenue INR 573 crore (+13.6% YoY, +24.5% QoQ), EBITDA incl. other income INR 38.8 crore at 6.7% margin, and PAT INR 20.5 crore. FY26 revenue rose about 23% to INR 1,912 crore, but absolute EBITDA and PAT declined YoY due to US tariffs escalating from 10% to 50% during 2025. Management redirected volumes to domestic demand, which grew about 27%, and retained a US presence at sub-economic margins. The Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore, Phase 1) is the main growth lever, with a stated INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition by FY31.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Grew 37.3% to INR 1,001 crore in FY26, led by power cables; domestic order book at INR 508 crore (87% of order book).

segments.name: Domestic B2C and distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 10.6% to INR 179 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Domestic B2G (government/PSU)
segments.commentary: Stable at about INR 182 crore in FY26, so its share of revenue fell.

segments.name: Exports (USA-led)
segments.commentary: Grew 13.9% to INR 550 crore in FY26 despite tariffs; eight active US distributors versus two in FY22.

guidance_outlook: FY27 (informal, assuming current metal prices hold): top-line growth of 15-20% and at least 10% volume growth; no formal guidance given.
Margins expected to return to FY25 levels as a first milestone, with pre-tariff margin levels targeted by end of FY27.

Narmadapuram Phase 1: investment about INR 300 crore by FY28; partial operations from Q1 FY28; sales target about INR 500 crore in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore in FY29; expected 9-10% margin and 3-4 year payback.

Long-term aspiration: INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31, implying doubling every 3-4 years; Phase 1 capacity alone seen at INR 3,600-4,000 crore, with Phase 2 (INR 200-300 crore capex) to exceed INR 5,000 crore.
Working capital expected to normalise within Q1 FY27 after receivables rose on Q4 back-ended dispatches.
capex_capacity: Two existing plants at Dharuhera (Haryana) and Kushkhera (Rajasthan) described as running at optimal utilisation for three to four years; physical space constraint reached.
Existing-plant capex of about INR 50-55 crore a year, over INR 160 crore across the past three years.

Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh): about 31 acres allotted by MPIDC and possession taken; civil works underway; long-lead machinery ordered; building construction to start shortly; commissioning from FY28.

Narmadapuram products: EHV cables up to 132 kV (starting with 33 kV, then 66 kV and 132 kV), transmission conductors, elastomeric EBeam and EPR cables, lead-sheathed rubber cables; EHV approvals expected by FY28.

Funding: about INR 122 crore of equity raised (about INR 92 crore from investors, about INR 30 crore from promoters), plus internal accruals and modest debt; current debt only about INR 110 crore of working capital limits.
demand_pricing: Management cites six demand drivers: India T&D capex of INR 3.35 lakh crore (FY26-30), renewables (210-220 GW solar and 50-60 GW wind by FY30), data centres (about 70% higher cable density for AI facilities), US grid capex above USD 1 trillion, construction capex of INR 18-19 lakh crore, and railways (FY27 budget INR 3 lakh crore).

US tariffs: 10% reciprocal tariff from 2 Apr 2025, raised to 25% in August and 50% by end-August 2025; IEEPA tariffs invalidated by US Supreme Court (Feb-Apr 2026), which management says restored India's competitiveness.
Management says it kept US presence at sub-economic margins at lower volumes; competitors from Vietnam, South Korea, Cambodia, Ecuador and Egypt had a tariff advantage in FY26.
Pricing policy: no firm-price orders with delivery beyond 3-4 months; metal is bought the next working day after order receipt; price-variation formulas increasingly accepted by customers.
Management expects Q2 FY27 onwards to see stronger US demand pull, with one or two new products to be launched in the US next quarter.
Middle East, Europe, Australia and Africa flagged as opportunistic markets, with the Middle East a focus area in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new plant reach optimum utilisation, and what is the payback and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 (INR 300 crore) targets INR 1,200 crore revenue by FY29; payback 3-4 years; margin 9-10%. No formal guidance, but 15-20% top-line growth and at least 10% volume growth assumed if metal prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the domestic market not scaled up the top line or bottom line over the past year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is capacity, not demand; the plants have run at full utilisation for four years, and the company diverted US volume to domestic. FY24 precedent: US sales fell from INR 400 crore to INR 280 crore while domestic doubled from INR 400 crore to INR 800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables roughly double, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 65% of Q4 sales were dispatched in the second half of the quarter; over three-quarters had been realised by 15 May 2026. Working capital cycle moved only from 99 to 101 days; CFO said most dispatches are against LCs.

qa_highlights.question: Can Paramount return to FY25 margins, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 EBITDA margin is the first milestone. Drivers: new products, US tariff normalisation, power, renewable and data-centre demand, and operating leverage on volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will EHV lead times exceed 5-6 months, and how is raw material risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids long-delivery firm-price orders and prefers 3-4 month horizons or price-variation clauses; EHV would follow the same policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the longer-term aspirational revenue and margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore by FY31; Phase 1 capacity can reach about INR 3,600-4,000 crore, and Phase 2 to exceed INR 5,000 crore. Margins expected to move towards peer range as scale grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet has low leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity was about INR 122 crore of the INR 300 crore project; management said it diversifies the funding mix, with working capital needs still to be bank-funded and current debt about INR 110 crore.

risks_watch: Receivables: working capital cycle at 101 days; management says receivables normalise in Q1 FY27 with over three-quarters of Q4 receivables already collected. Watch the Q1 FY27 receivable run-rate.
US tariff regime and recovery: margins in the US remain below pre-tariff levels; watch whether volumes and margins improve each quarter from Q2 FY27.
Narmadapuram execution: commissioning slated for Q1 FY28 with EHV approvals expected by FY28; the 9-10% margin and INR 1,200 crore FY29 target depend on it.
Raw material (copper and aluminium) pass-through: policy is to avoid long firm-price orders, but EHV and longer-cycle orders may test this.
Management's FY31 INR 5,000 crore target and the FY27 guidance are informal and conditional on metal prices holding.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand, US recovery and Narmadapuram, while openly acknowledging a difficult FY26. Answers on receivables and FY27 guidance were less precise, with management declining formal guidance and the CFO deferring current cash figures.

growth.why: Informal FY27 guidance of 15-20% top-line growth (minimum 10% volume) rests on a record INR 583 crore order book (power cable orders INR 466 crore, +66%) and strong domestic demand, while the main long-term lever, Narmadapuram (INR 300 crore), only starts partial operations in Q1 FY28, so FY27 growth relies mainly on existing plants running at optimal utilisation.
